Bumps [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) from 0.3.0 to 0.5.0.
Release notes

Sourced from lino-arguments's releases.

[Rust] 0.5.0

Changed

  • Updated Rust CI/CD workflow to match best practices from rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
  • Added detect-changes job for conditional job execution based on file changes
  • Added version-check job to prevent manual version modification in PRs
  • Added crates.io publishing support with CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN or CARGO_TOKEN
  • Added changelog-pr manual release mode for review-based releases
  • Added multi-language repository support via rust-paths.mjs utility
  • Improved job conditions using always() && !cancelled() pattern for proper dependency handling

Added

  • scripts/rust-paths.mjs - Core utility for auto-detecting Rust package root in multi-language repos
  • scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs - File change detection for conditional CI/CD job execution
  • scripts/check-version-modification.mjs - Prevents manual version changes in PRs
  • scripts/check-changelog-fragment.mjs - Validates changelog fragments in pull requests
  • scripts/git-config.mjs - Git user configuration utility for CI/CD
  • scripts/get-bump-type.mjs - Determines version bump type from changelog fragment frontmatter
  • scripts/check-release-needed.mjs - Checks if a release should proceed
  • scripts/get-version.mjs - Extracts version from Cargo.toml
  • scripts/collect-changelog.mjs - Collects and processes changelog fragments
  • scripts/create-changelog-fragment.mjs - Creates changelog fragments for manual releases
  • scripts/publish-crate.mjs - Publishes package to crates.io with multi-repo support

Added

  • LinoParser trait extending clap's Parser — lino_parse() automatically loads .lenv and .env files before CLI parsing
  • Full support for #[arg(long, env = "PORT", default_value = "3000")] with automatic .lenv/.env resolution
  • lino_parse_with(), lino_parse_from(), lino_parse_from_with() methods for custom file paths and testing
  • load_env_file() and load_env_file_override() for standard .env file support via dotenvy
  • .env() and .env_override() methods on ConfigBuilder for functional API
  • Re-exported clap derive macros (Parser, Args, Subcommand, ValueEnum) for struct-based CLI parsing without a separate clap dependency
  • make_config() functional builder API inspired by the JavaScript makeConfig function
  • make_config_from() for testing with custom arguments
  • Config type with .get(), .get_int(), .get_bool(), and .has() accessors
  • ConfigBuilder with chainable .option(), .flag(), .lenv(), .env(), .name(), .about(), .version() methods
  • Examples for both struct-based and functional usage patterns

Added

  • Integration with lino-env crate (v0.1.0) for reading .lenv configuration files
  • New load_lenv_file() function to load environment variables from .lenv files
  • New load_lenv_file_override() function to load and overwrite existing environment variables
  • Re-exported LinoEnv, read_lino_env, and write_lino_env from lino-env crate
  • CLI now supports --configuration flag to load configuration from .lenv files

Added

  • Crates.io version badge to rust/README.md and root README.md for easy visibility of published Rust package version
  • docs.rs documentation badge to rust/README.md and root README.md
  • Rust CI status badge to rust/README.md

Bumps [regex](https://github.com/rust-lang/regex) from 1.12.3 to 1.13.1.
Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

body:
Fixes #239

The example's pinned Rust image could age silently because no dependency updater covered it. Update `rust:1.96.0-slim` to the published `rust:1.100.0-slim` tag and multi-platform digest, and enable weekly Dependabot updates with seven-day cooldowns for Docker, GitHub Actions, Cargo and npm CI tooling.

The offline coverage check parses tracked Dockerfiles and dependency manifests, requires an update entry for each populated surface, and rejects empty entries, disabled updates and unsupported exclusions. It covers every registry `FROM`, handles prior stages/scratch, platform options, continuations, heredocs and ARG image references, and supports exact `directory` and `directories` entries. Dependency-free example manifests do not create empty jobs. The existing Node-enabled CI job runs the new guard and its regressions on every run and feeds the terminal pipeline status.

Reproduction and verification:

- Before: the original Dockerfile used Rust 1.96.0 and `.github/dependabot.yml` was absent. The regression reproduces missing configuration and uncovered images in an isolated Git repository; adding the correct entry passes, and adding another nested Dockerfile fails again.
- Eight focused regressions cover directory coverage, every external stage, empty ecosystems, YAML errors and update bypasses. The repository check covers 14 populated surfaces.
- On `ea7bffb`: all 133 JavaScript tests pass, including the new policy tests and existing native/gate tests. Native example parity and regenerate-and-diff checks, the root JavaScript detection gate, formatting, required documentation and workflow tool installation checks pass. Docker Hub's published multi-platform digest was verified with `docker buildx imagetools inspect` without downloading layers.
- All six workflows pass on the same `ea7bffb` revision: [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783331), [JavaScript-first example](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783235), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783233), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783242), [Desktop Release](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783282), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540783231). This includes Linux/macOS/Windows tests, Clippy, full release-script tests, packaging, merge simulation, the example container, and the new dependency policy steps. Dependabot configuration validation also passes. No CI failures required another batch.

The [requirement inventory and assumptions](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-239-c880158efbe4/docs/issue-239-plan.md) document the four supported ecosystems and deliberately exact coverage semantics. The root has no production JavaScript counterpart; existing example inventory and acceptance assertions are preserved. A patch changelog fragment prepares the existing automated release trigger. Current main is included; no merge or release is performed.

body:
Fixes #237
Fixes #234
Fixes #235
Fixes #236

PR code changes now remain covered after a docs-only follow-up. Link checks include timeouts and refuse checker crashes/configuration errors; CodeQL reports every malformed item, diagnostic and finding with safely quoted fields. PR jobs restore caches without saving them, JavaScript helpers receive source-size limits, pinned ShellCheck runs from a venv, and independent sibling-language releases no longer strand a Rust release.

The complete requirement inventory, root causes, alternatives, component research, assumptions and verification mapping are in [docs/issue-237.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-237-697906e36048/docs/issue-237.md). Every listed sub-issue is implemented here; no requirement was already resolved or deferred.

Reproduction and regression coverage:

- #234: a runner with system ShellCheck triggers the old pipx PATH warning. The workflow invokes the same pinned distribution from an isolated venv; policy assertions and actual ShellCheck verify it.
- #235: create a code commit followed by a docs commit, then a synthetic PR merge. The detector now compares base-to-merge; its regression asserts both files. The orphan rename fixture now explicitly performs its intended source deletion in the merged tree, preserving all original acceptance assertions.
- #236 links: a recovered 503 beside a timeout previously opened the gate without checking the timeout. Both sections now reach both consumers; tests cover timeout-only reports, incomplete totals and exit 1/3 refusal. A weekly schedule detects link rot.
- #236 CodeQL: SARIF with malformed records, diagnostics, findings and embedded CR/LF workflow commands now produces all problems on safe log lines across every report. Malformed objects that shadow `toString` cannot interrupt aggregation; that regression also fails before its fix.
- #236 caches: repository-wide policy tests cover every active restore/save and both Docker exporters. Only successful main pushes save a missed cache. Fresh-merge only restores compatible lint caches; lychee keys depend on inputs.
- #236 size: real `.mjs`/`.js` files at 900/901/1001 lines exercise the existing warning/hard-limit checker; documentation limits remain intact.
- #236 releases: actual local Git origins and a mock registry cover JS Changeset consumption and Python/C# version writes, initially and during a push race. Rust source/dependency changes, shared CI/tooling, root manifests, edited fragments and external path dependencies remain refused. Repository-root packages retain whole-tree validation; nested-root independence assumptions are documented.

Validation on `82e59df`: full script suite (including 120 JavaScript tests and offline Git/registry integrations), 291 Rust CI policy tests, Clippy for all targets/features, Cargo manifest warning gate, formatting, file sizes, workflow tool installation checks, actionlint and actual pinned ShellCheck all pass. Before/after regression runs confirm the original link/CodeQL defects and malformed-object failure. All five workflows pass on the exact same revision: [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43399281745), [Desktop Release](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43399281924), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43399282054), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43399281738), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43399281804). Current `main` is included and the working tree is clean. The first CI batch passed main, desktop, security and workflow validation; its sole failure was a wrong upstream URL in the new research document, corrected here (run 43397905111, log lines 627 and 647). The root automatic JavaScript gate reports no production counterpart; tooling does not require a port. A patch changelog fragment prepares the automated release trigger without manually changing package versions.
